title: Turn the dial down fast
subtitle: When distress is very high, the quickest way back is through the body.

steps.body:
When distress is very high, the fastest way back is through the body, not the mind.

Four quick options below — use any that fit. If you're in danger or crisis, please reach out to a person now; the Support tab has crisis lines.

Cold.

Hold something cold — splash cool water on your face, hold ice, step into cooler air. A sharp temperature change calms the body's alarm surprisingly fast.

Move.

Thirty seconds of intense movement — jumping jacks, a fast walk, running up stairs — burns off the surge of stress chemicals so they stop circling.

Breathe.

Slow your exhale longer than your inhale. Follow the circle for a few rounds — in as it grows, out as it shrinks.

Release.

Tense your shoulders hard for five seconds, then let go completely. Notice the difference. Do it anywhere you're holding.
You used your body to turn the dial down. If the distress stays very high, that's a signal to reach out to a person — the Support tab is there for exactly this.

exit.body: You did something kind and practical for a nervous system in alarm. That's enough for right now.
